overview: Scott Technology is a 110+ year old Dunedin, New Zealand-founded designer and manufacturer of automation and robotics systems, operating across four domains: Protein/meat processing (lamb, beef, poultry, BladeStop bandsaw safety), Materials Handling & Logistics (end-of-line palletizing, AGVs, ASRS, Maestro+ software), Mining/Minerals (Rocklabs sample preparation equipment), and Appliances (turn-key assembly lines for global whiteware makers). The company operates through manufacturing/engineering hubs in New Zealand, Australia, China, Europe and North America, serving 350+ customers in 30+ countries. Its single largest shareholder is JBS Australia (part of JBS S.A., the world's largest meat processor), which holds a controlling stake (~54% as of mid-2026), making Scott both a global automation vendor and a partly captive supplier to its own majority owner.

business_model.summary: Scott earns revenue from three streams: bespoke engineered Projects (~50-56% of revenue historically, design-to-install, built on customer trust and long lead times), repeatable Products (standard/modular equipment such as Rocklabs sample-prep units and BladeStop, lower risk and higher margin, ~16-20%), and Service/aftermarket (installation servicing, consumables, upgrades, software licensing - now the fastest growing and highest quality stream). Group gross/net margin has expanded from roughly 13% (FY2020) to 27% (FY2024) to 29% (FY2025/HY26) as the mix has shifted toward products and service. Group EBITDA margin (EBITDA/revenue) sits around 10-12%, well below the net-margin figure because net margin is calculated only on direct/indirect cost of goods (excludes overheads).

revenue_streams.name: Materials Handling & Logistics (MHL)
revenue_streams.notes: FY24 basis; HY26 revenue $65m (+21% YoY), 26% net margin, largest and fastest-growing domain, Europe-centred with expanding US/Australia footprint

revenue_streams.name: Protein
revenue_streams.notes: FY24 basis; HY26 revenue $28m (-8% YoY) on delayed customer capex decisions; historically ~28-36% net margin, highest service penetration (55% of revenue at HY26)

revenue_streams.name: Mining (Rocklabs)
revenue_streams.notes: FY24 basis; HY26 revenue $26m (+9% YoY); highest-margin domain (37% net margin HY26, historically up to 40-46%), driven by gold price strength and standard product/consumables sales

revenue_streams.name: Appliances
revenue_streams.notes: FY24 basis; HY26 revenue $10m (-28% YoY) on project cycling/design-phase timing; China-centred (Qingdao Centre of Excellence), lumpy $20m+ projects with GEA, Sub-Zero, Midea

revenue_streams.name: Service/Aftermarket (cross-domain)
revenue_streams.notes: HY26: 33% of total group revenue, up from 24% in HY22; the strategic centrepiece of Destination 2030 - recurring, higher-margin, tied to installed base growth

business_model.customer_type: B2B, large multinational enterprise customers - global protein processors (JBS, other majors), FMCG/consumer goods manufacturers (PepsiCo, Danone, Essity, Bakker), mining majors and labs (Rio Tinto, SGS, Kinross Gold, MRL), and global appliance OEMs (Midea, GEA, Sub-Zero). Revenue is project-based and lumpy for large engineered systems, blended with a growing recurring service/consumables layer.
business_model.geographic_mix: HY26 revenue by manufacturing region: Europe ~43% ($54.8m), Americas ~21% ($26.6m), Rocklabs (global mining) ~20% ($25.0m), Australia ~9% ($11.8m), China ~4% ($5.4m), New Zealand ~4% ($4.5m). Reporting currency is NZD; the large offshore revenue base creates material currency translation exposure.

main_competitors: JBT Marel (formed Jan 2025 from JBT Corp's acquisition of Marel) - dominant scaled competitor across primary/secondary protein processing and packaging
Frontmatec - red meat (pork/beef) slaughter automation specialist
Bettcher Industries - handheld cutting/trimming tools for meat processing
GEA Group - broad food processing and packaging technology
Dematic, Swisslog, Knapp, Vanderlande - large-scale materials handling/warehouse automation (Scott's MHL unit is subscale relative to these global integrators)
SGS, ALS and in-house mining lab automation efforts - indirect competition for Rocklabs, though Scott states it faces limited direct competition in several of its niche/patented product lines
competitive_position.market_position: Global niche leader in narrow, technically difficult sub-segments (BladeStop bandsaw safety, automated lamb boning/primal processing, poultry trussing, mining sample-prep via Rocklabs) rather than a broad-line leader. Subscale versus the newly combined JBT Marel in protein and versus Dematic/Swisslog/Vanderlande in materials handling, where Scott is still building a US reference-site base.

moat_factors.description: BladeStop (fastest-stopping bandsaw, <10ms, versus >20ms nearest competitor, 1,500+ units in 30 countries), the only commercial automated lamb boning system, world-first automated poultry trussing - management states these face no direct competitor

Majority owner JBS (world's largest meat processor) is also a customer and reference site (e.g. the large JBS Brooks Canada MHL project), giving Scott privileged access and a proof point, but this is a related party, not a fully independent commercial relationship
Growing service/consumables revenue (33% of group revenue at HY26, up from 24% in HY22) reflects rising switching costs and recurring economics as the installed base of equipment grows

moat_factors.factor: Rocklabs brand and market position in sample-prep
moat_factors.description: 50+ years operating history in mining sample preparation, internationally recognised certified reference materials, highest-margin domain in the group
Manufacturing centres of excellence in NZ, Australia, Europe, China and North America support multi-region delivery, but scale in MHL/Appliances remains well below global leaders

weaknesses: Subscale in Materials Handling and Appliances relative to global players (Dematic, Vanderlande, JBT Marel) - management itself flagged 'sales have plateaued' pre-Destination 2030
Protein domain innovation historically project-led rather than platform-led; beef automation still in development with no released product
Heavy reliance on large, lumpy engineered projects creates working capital volatility and revenue unpredictability quarter to quarter
Low free float (~46% of shares) and majority-owner governance reduce independent-shareholder influence and can suppress valuation multiples
Newly combined JBT Marel (Jan-2025 merger) materially increases scale of Scott's largest protein-sector competitor

growth_drivers: Destination 2030 strategy - refreshed FY2025, targeting '$530m by 30' revenue (~11-14% CAGR from FY25's $275m) and 14% EBITDA margin by FY30, built around four enablers: Customer First, One Scott, Leading-Edge Technology, High-Performing Teams
Domain-level FY24-FY30 CAGR targets set at Investor Day: Protein 16-20%, MHL 7-11%, Mining 6-10%, Appliances 3-7%
Service/lifecycle revenue mix expansion - targeted at 35%+ of group revenue by FY30 (from 28-33% currently), providing recurring, higher-margin income

MHL North American expansion - NexBot AGV platform launched in Chicago; two large US reference sites going live in calendar 2025/26 to anchor further US wins; first Australian MHL contract secured (Farm Frites) expanding beyond the European base

Protein value-chain extension - accelerating beef and lamb prototypes toward commercialisation (beef automation has no current competing solution due to technical complexity); Poultry Trusser expansion in North America; BladeStop market-share growth globally including non-protein industrial applications (adopted by two German car manufacturers)

Mining/Rocklabs expansion - Automated Modular System (AMS) targeting blue-chip customers, RoboFuel and Energize field-automation products, new North American direct sales presence (Canada + US service), AI/data integration (Maestro+ software) opportunity
Appliances - large China-anchored contracts (Midea, GEA, Sub-Zero) and a $44m Americas project win for FY26 expanding beyond the historical China base

Forward work book recovery - grew from $165m (HY25) to $177m (HY26), with $40m of new MHL contracts (EU, North America, Australia) plus a second LEAP lamb-primal contract win in Australia and a US whiteware appliance order, supporting a stronger H2 FY26

business.description: HY26 Protein revenue fell 8% on delayed customer capital investment decisions and soft BladeStop volumes; management is relying on recent wins (Australian lamb primal contract) to deliver a stronger H2

Large engineered contracts (some individually $20m+, e.g. Appliances projects) create quarter-to-quarter revenue and margin volatility; forward work book has swung from $195m (FY23) to $160m (FY24) to $177m (HY26)
The January 2025 merger of JBT and Marel created a much larger, more capitalised competitor across the entire protein processing value chain

WorkSafe New Zealand charged Scott Technology in May 2026 (maximum penalty NZ$1.5m) following the fatal workplace death of PLC technician Michael Sherry at the Dunedin site in April 2025; reputational and execution risk for a company whose products are marketed on safety credentials (BladeStop)
CFO Mark O'Malley (in role since July 2023) announced departure effective 3 July 2026; successor not yet publicly named as of the H1-26 result

financial.description: Operating cash flow is volatile and project-timing dependent - swung from $(8.8)m (HY22) to $26.0m (HY23) to $6.1m (HY26); FY24 operating cash flow fell to $6.0m from $20.2m in FY23 due to project payment timing

~90%+ of revenue is generated outside New Zealand (Europe ~43%, Americas ~21%, Rocklabs/global mining ~20% of HY26 revenue) while reporting is in NZD, creating translation volatility (FX reserve moved from +$4.5m to $(1.7)m in HY26 alone)

Net debt was $13.1m at HY26 (broadly stable); total lease liabilities (current + non-current) of ~$31.1m reflect IFRS 16 treatment of expanding global facilities, adding to reported depreciation and finance costs that compress NPAT even when EBITDA is stable

financial.risk: Gap between EBITDA and NPAT growth
financial.description: FY2024: EBITDA was flat/resilient ($26.4m reported, $30.2m operating) but NPAT fell 50% to $7.7m due to $3.8m one-off strategic review/restructuring costs, higher lease costs from facility expansion, higher effective interest rates on debt, and an adverse NZ tax-legislation change removing building depreciation deductibility - illustrates that headline EBITDA understates the below-the-line cost sensitivity of the P&L

regulatory.description: Active WorkSafe prosecution in New Zealand (2026) with potential fine and reputational impact; company is investing materially in a 'OneScott HSWE' safety system overhaul in FY26
NZ change removing building depreciation deductibility was a direct, one-off contributor to the FY2024 NPAT decline

JBS's stake (~54%) sits near thresholds that interact with the NZX Takeovers Code; the 2023 strategic review (Macquarie Capital engaged) explored ownership options but concluded without a transaction, after costing the company ~$2.4m; JBS has instead continued to creep its holding upward via participation in the dividend reinvestment plan

macro.description: Management explicitly flagged in the HY26 result and outlook that 'recent geopolitical events' could affect customer capital investment decisions and that guidance assumes no material escalation; US/China tariff dynamics are relevant given significant Americas and China revenue exposure

Protein and mining customer capex cycles are the primary demand drivers for Scott's largest-margin domains; Mining benefited from favourable gold/copper prices in HY26 (a tailwind that could reverse), while Protein customers are currently delaying investment decisions - the two cycles are not obviously correlated, providing some natural diversification but also meaning weakness can appear in either domain independently

macro.risk: Global automation capex sensitivity to interest rates and recession risk
macro.description: Large engineered automation projects are discretionary capital expenditure for customers and can be deferred in a higher-rate or slower-growth environment, as evidenced by delayed Protein customer decisions in HY26

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global industrial automation and robotics demand is supported by structural labour shortages, reshoring, food-safety/traceability requirements, and rising wage costs in protein processing, materials handling, and mining. Management cites the MHL addressable market alone at over US$20bn by 2030.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - order in-take and project timing are tied to customer capital expenditure cycles in protein processing, consumer packaged goods manufacturing, and mining/commodity price cycles; growing service/recurring revenue (33% of group revenue at HY26) is dampening cyclicality over time.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - customer capex decisions for large discretionary automation projects are rate-sensitive (evidenced by delayed Protein investment decisions in HY26); Scott's own balance sheet carries modest net debt (~$13m) and lease liabilities (~$31m) sensitive to funding costs.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High - the large majority of revenue is generated in EUR, USD, AUD and other currencies outside New Zealand while consolidated reporting is in NZD, creating material translation risk to reported results.
key_input_costs: Skilled engineering labour (a persistent constraint globally)

recent_developments.event: Investor Day (ID25) held in Auckland; Destination 2030 strategy formally launched externally, including the $530m FY30 revenue target and 14% EBITDA margin target

FY2025 full-year results released: record operating EBITDA of $31.5m (+19% YoY), NPAT of $14.2m (+84% YoY), revenue flat at $275m ($276m in FY24), net margin improved to 29%, net debt reduced 39% to $12.3m, full-year dividend 8.0 cents

HY26 results released: EBITDA $13.0m (+7% YoY), revenue $128m (+5%), MHL +21%, Mining +9%, Protein -8% and Appliances -28% (project timing), service revenue reached 33% of total, forward work grew to $177m from $165m, interim dividend declared at 4.0 cents per share
WorkSafe New Zealand filed a charge against Scott Technology over the April 2025 workplace death of PLC technician Michael Sherry at the Dunedin site; maximum potential fine NZ$1.5 million

JBS Australia increased its Scott Technology shareholding to 54.06% (45,894,965 of 84,892,648 shares) via participation in the dividend reinvestment plan, up from 53.05% previously - a gradual creep in the controlling stake rather than a formal takeover offer
CFO Mark O'Malley announced his resignation, departing 3 July 2026 after joining in July 2023; a successor search is underway and had not been publicly resolved as of the HY26 result date

Company issued market guidance for record FY2026 revenue of $290-296m and record operating EBITDA of $34-36m, citing continued Destination 2030 execution progress - could not independently verify the exact announcement date via primary NZX source; sourced from BusinessDesk/TradingView coverage

guidance.as_of: HY26 Results (15 April 2026) and subsequent market update reported in web coverage

items.notes: Would represent growth versus FY2025's $275m; sourced from secondary web coverage (BusinessDesk/TradingView), not independently confirmed against a primary NZX announcement text - flagged as unverified precision on exact date
Would represent growth versus FY2025's record $31.5m operating EBITDA; same sourcing caveat as revenue guidance above

items.target: Positively weighted second half, similar pattern to FY2025
items.notes: Management guided to a stronger H2 in the HY26 presentation, citing recent contract wins across Protein, MHL and Appliances, and forward work growth to $177m, explicitly conditioned on 'recent geopolitical events' not escalating materially

Implies an ~11% CAGR from FY25 revenue of $275m per the FY25 annual report letter; the CEO separately described it in his address as a '14% CAGR from FY25' figure - the two disclosures are not fully reconciled, flagged for the user's attention
Up from ~11.5% (HY26 run-rate) and 11.1% FY25 reported EBITDA margin ($31.5m/$275m); management frames delivery as 'non-linear from a financial performance perspective'
Up from 33% at HY26 and 28-29% in FY24/FY25
Disclosed at Investor Day; Protein is the highest-growth-targeted domain despite being the weakest performer in HY26, underscoring execution risk

Dividends considered semi-annually; DRP offered; FY25 total dividend was 8.0 cents (5.0 cents final + 3.0 cents interim), consistent with FY24's 8.0 cents total; HY26 interim dividend of 4.0 cents (unimputed) was higher than HY25's 3.0 cents

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Mike Christman has repeatedly stated Destination 2030 is 'driving results faster than expected' (FY25 annual report) and that the business is seeing a 'hockey stick effect' in early execution (per H1 FY26 earnings call coverage). Management's HY26 outlook flagged: improved operating leverage and a stronger H2 expected (as in FY25), contingent on recent geopolitical volatility not escalating; mitigating actions are in place for tariff/trade risk to the extent possible; and progress toward the FY30 target 'remains on track... albeit non-linear.' Scott does not provide formal point-estimate guidance in its investor materials as a matter of policy, instead pointing to the forward work book ($177m at HY26) as the primary leading indicator - the specific FY26 revenue/EBITDA numeric guidance found in web coverage should be treated as a discrete market update rather than standing policy.

bull_case: Multi-year gross/net margin expansion story (13% in FY2020 to 29% at HY26) driven by a genuine mix shift toward higher-margin products and recurring service revenue, which is structurally less lumpy and more valuable per dollar of revenue than legacy bespoke engineering projects

Destination 2030 provides a credible, well-articulated growth roadmap with quantified targets ($530m revenue, 14% EBITDA margin, 35%+ service mix by FY30) and management is showing early tangible progress (record FY25 EBITDA and NPAT, growing forward work book to $177m)

JBS's ~54% ownership provides a captive reference customer and channel-validation (e.g. the large JBS Brooks Canada MHL project) that a purely independent automation vendor of Scott's size would struggle to access, while also creating latent takeover optionality for minority holders if JBS ever moves to a full buyout

Genuinely differentiated, patented technology in narrow niches (BladeStop's <10ms stopping time versus >20ms nearest competitor; the only commercial automated lamb boning system) gives real pricing power and limited direct competition in several core product lines

Diversification across four domains with historically low correlation provided real earnings resilience in HY26 - MHL (+21%) and Mining (+9%) more than offset weakness in Protein (-8%) and Appliances (-28%), demonstrating the portfolio effect management is targeting
bear_case: Majority ownership by JBS (~54% and rising via DRP participation) means minority shareholders have limited influence over capital allocation, M&A, and strategic direction; the 2023 strategic review cost ~$2.4m and 'went nowhere,' evidencing both governance friction and the difficulty of unlocking a control premium for minorities

The FY2024 experience - flat/resilient EBITDA but a 50% collapse in NPAT - shows headline EBITDA growth can mask a fragile bottom line vulnerable to one-off costs, rising lease/interest expense, and adverse tax changes; investors focused only on EBITDA risk overestimating cash earnings power

Newly merged JBT Marel (Jan 2025) materially increases the scale and R&D firepower of Scott's largest identifiable competitor in the protein-processing space, its most profitable growth-targeted domain (16-20% FY24-30 CAGR target)

Protein segment - the domain with the highest targeted growth rate - is currently the weakest performer (HY26 revenue -8%) due to delayed customer capital investment, illustrating the gap between strategic ambition and near-term execution and creating real risk the FY30 targets are not met on schedule

Small-cap NZX illiquidity, low free float (majority locked up with JBS), project-based revenue lumpiness, and an active WorkSafe prosecution (following an April 2025 workplace fatality) create idiosyncratic risk on top of currency translation exposure from a predominantly offshore (Europe/Americas) revenue base reported in NZD
unverified_flags: The precise FY2026 revenue ($290-296m) and operating EBITDA ($34-36m) guidance figures and their exact announcement date were sourced from secondary web coverage (BusinessDesk headline via AI-generated summary, TradingView/Reuters headline) rather than a primary NZX filing text read directly; recommend confirming against the original NZX announcement before using in a dashboard.

The FY30 revenue CAGR is described inconsistently across sources - the FY25 Annual Report chairman's letter/five-year trend implies roughly 11% CAGR from FY25's $275m to $530m by FY30, while the CEO's own quoted commentary in the same annual report says '14% CAGR from FY25' - flagged rather than reconciled.
Could not independently verify the current CFO successor to Mark O'Malley (departing 3 July 2026) as no announcement of a named replacement was found in available web sources as of the analysis date.
